apps.internet: To fetch NASA's picture and the satellite images
apps.name: APOD Wallpaper

notes: Right after login or a wake, the new picture now waits for Wi-Fi and downloads as soon as the connection is back. Before, a download in those first seconds failed, and yesterday's picture (or an old Live Earth) stayed up for up to 20 minutes.

apps.summary: Sets your wallpaper to NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day, the latest whole-Earth satellite picture, a star chart drawn for where you are, or a solid colour.
apps.tagline: NASA's picture of the day, Live Earth or the night sky, as your wallpaper.

apps.name: Chào

notes: Launch at Login now always opens this copy in Applications. Before, a Mac could keep opening an old copy at login.

apps.summary: A word of the day in the menu bar, coloured by tone. Say it and see your pitch against the tone, practise with cards and tone drills, and keep a phrase sheet handy.
apps.tagline: A Southern Vietnamese word a day, with tone practice.

apps.name: Citrus
apps.needs: Some conversions need tools its installer adds: run Install Citrus.command from the Download zip once

notes: Check for Updates… in Citrus's menu. From now on Citrus updates itself, checking once a day.

apps.summary: Drag files with a modifier key held to convert them: images, documents, audio and video. Its installer adds the Homebrew tools it uses.
apps.tagline: Convert files by dragging onto a pop-up wheel.

apps.name: Equate
apps.needs: Screen Recording for snipping. Apple's second opinion needs macOS 27 with Apple Intelligence on; Equate works without it

notes: Snips now freeze the screen first, so what's inside your box is exactly what gets read (snips in some browsers were cut short on the right). The result panel has the usual close and minimise buttons.

apps.summary: Press ⌃⌥E and drag round an equation in a PDF, a web page or a picture. Equate reads it on your Mac and puts it on the clipboard in the best form for the app you're in: a real equation in Word and Google Docs, a sharp picture in Pages and Keynote, LaTeX everywhere else. It also reads PDFs, iPhone photos of the whiteboard and equations you write on the trackpad, and keeps a history. No account, no limit, nothing uploaded.
apps.tagline: Snip any equation, paste it as LaTeX, Word or Google Docs maths.

apps.licence: MIT, with teacher.dev's Apache-2.0 figure generators
apps.name: Figure It

notes: Coordinate grid: number an axis in π radians or degrees, with gridlines every π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2 or π for trig graphs. Fractions and π on the axes are stacked (3π over 2) so they never run into each other.

apps.summary: 73 figures for Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Maths and Economics. Change the numbers and labels, make a student copy and an answer key, make versions A, B and C, then drag the figure into Pages, Keynote or Google Docs.
apps.tagline: Figures for tests and worksheets, with student copies and answer keys.

apps.internet: Only Google Docs, to read a doc’s history as you, and update checks
apps.name: Footprints
apps.needs: Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, and edit access to the docs you check. Add its extension once with Load unpacked: the app shows how

notes: Every browser's setup steps now have Open Extensions, Show Folder and Copy Path buttons, and explain how to reach the extension's folder with ⌘⇧G (Command-Shift-G) in the Load unpacked window.

apps.summary: Open any Google Doc you can edit and click the Footprints button: watch the doc write itself again, with typed text, pastes from outside, moved text and text another student’s doc had first all marked, and see when the writer worked. Make a one-page PDF report, or check every doc linked on a Toddle assignment or Drive folder at once, so a paragraph that turns up in two students’ docs shows who had it first. Everything is worked out on your computer; nothing is sent anywhere.
apps.tagline: See how a Google Doc was written.

apps.name: FreeUp

notes: Clean Up: Cleaner (caches, logs, files of apps you removed), Uninstaller (an app with everything it left behind), Chat Downloads (old Zalo, WhatsApp and Telegram photos and videos) and Old Installers. Everything goes to the Trash after you see the list.

apps.summary: Scans a disk or folder and draws it as rings. Click to go in, drag what you don't need to be deleted, and see the space come back. Clean Up clears caches, old chat downloads and installers, and uninstalls apps with everything they left behind.
apps.tagline: See what fills your disk, on a sunburst map.

apps.internet: Only for radio, MusicBrainz and the Internet Archive
apps.licence: MIT, with LGPL libraries (FFmpeg, libbluray, dsd-nexus)
apps.name: HD Music
apps.summary: Plays DSF, DFF, SACD ISOs, Blu-ray audio and hi-res files bit-perfect, with a signal path and converter, an EQ that corrects your headphones (from AutoEQ's measurements) and can work on every app's sound, a library for local drives and NAS shares, internet radio and the Internet Archive.
apps.tagline: Hi-res and DSD player, with a library, radio and EQ.

apps.name: Hem

notes: Check for Updates… at the bottom of Hem's panel. From now on Hem updates itself, checking once a day.

apps.summary: Slide along an edge of the trackpad to change the volume, the screen or keyboard brightness, or scrub what's playing. Tap then slide for a second action.
apps.tagline: Volume and brightness sliders on your trackpad's edges.

apps.internet: Only a one-time download of each language, for translating (by the browser) and for talk and type (by macOS), and update checks
apps.name: Lamplight
apps.needs: Google Chrome 138 or Microsoft Edge 148 or newer. Add its extension once with Load unpacked: the app shows how. Simpler words need Apple Intelligence (macOS 26 or later)
apps.summary: Lamplight reads any web page, Google Doc or PDF aloud in Chrome or Edge, lighting up each word as it goes. Double-click a word for its picture, pronunciation, a simple meaning and the word in Vietnamese, Korean, Chinese or Japanese; translate a sentence or a whole page; open it in a calm reader with the translation under each paragraph; and keep words in a word bank to practise. With the app running, students can talk and type in English or their own language, and on Macs with Apple Intelligence, rewrite a hard sentence in simpler words. Reading, translating, talk and type and simpler words all happen on the computer, with no account.
apps.tagline: Reading help for students learning English.

apps.name: Pigeonhole
apps.needs: Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Add its extension once with Load unpacked: Settings › Browsers shows how

notes: If a space changed on your other Mac while it was open here and you leave it without answering "Use theirs" or "Keep this window's", the tabs you changed in this window now stay, and the other Mac's copy is kept in the space's History. The question also goes away by itself once the window has the same tabs as the other copy.

apps.summary: Give each project its own space of tabs in Chrome and Edge. Switch a window to a space and its tabs come back as you left them; everything is saved as you browse, with history. Pigeonhole's page, the first tab of every window, lists all your spaces and their tabs. Spaces follow you to your other Mac through iCloud Drive.
apps.tagline: Spaces of tabs for Chrome and Edge.

apps.name: Rummage
apps.needs: Searching by meaning needs macOS 15 and an Apple Silicon Mac, and a one-time download of its reading model (about 0.9 GB)

notes: The toolbar's eye, box and trash icons are gone: set invisible items, package contents and the Trash with the pickers under the rules.

apps.summary: Find any file by its name, dates, size, kind, tags, contents and more, straight from the disk with no index, and several times faster than a one-folder-at-a-time search in your home folder. Turn on Rummage and it also finds files by what they're about: a sentence like “the worksheet with the skateboard on the ramp” finds the PDF, the scan or the photo, read on your Mac and never uploaded. Opens Find Any File's saved searches.
apps.tagline: Find any file, even by what's in it.

apps.name: Scrawl

notes: Check for Updates… in Scrawl's menu. From now on Scrawl updates itself, checking once a day.

apps.summary: Capture an area, a window or the whole screen from the menu bar, then mark it up with arrows, shapes, text, highlights and blur.
apps.tagline: Screenshots with arrows, text and blur.

apps.name: Shunt
apps.needs: Accessibility, and Mission Control’s “Move left/right a space” shortcuts left on (they are unless you changed them). Throw for AirPlay TVs; Pigeonhole for a tab to join a Chrome or Edge window already there

notes: Incognito windows: moving a tab now always takes it from the window you're in, as a new incognito window. Shunt only hands tab moves to Pigeonhole 1.7.2 or later, which never guesses which window you meant.

apps.summary: Press ⌃⌘→ and the window you’re using slides to the next Space with you; ⌃⌘↑ puts it on another screen or an AirPlay TV, and ⌃⌘↓ brings it back. Add ⇧ to move just the browser tab (or every tab you’ve selected), or ⌥⇧ to move it on its own, without any pinned tabs. A small map shows where it went, and ⌃⌘Z puts it back.
apps.tagline: Send a window, or just a tab, to another Space or screen with one key.

apps.name: Signpost

notes: Cleans links as you copy them: tracking tags come out and redirects are unwrapped, with the same settings as links you open. Passwords and text that's more than a link are left alone, and the menu can put the original back.

apps.summary: Each time you open a link or an HTML file, choose the browser and the profile from a list right by the pointer. Tracking tags come out and redirect links are unwrapped, in links you open and links you copy, and the menu keeps your recent links.
apps.tagline: Choose the browser and profile for every link.

apps.name: SmartCut

notes: Launch at Login now always opens this copy in Applications. Before, a Mac could keep opening an old copy at login.

apps.summary: Hold ⌘ and a panel lists the front app's keyboard shortcuts, including Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and Gmail in your browser. Type to filter, and find hotkeys that clash.
apps.tagline: Hold ⌘ to see every shortcut in the app you're using.

apps.name: Storefront

notes: Right after login or a wake, Storefront now waits for Wi-Fi before checking for updates, and checks again as soon as the connection is back. Before, a check in those first seconds said you were offline, and the next one was hours away.
Opens at login only from the copy in Applications, never from a spare copy elsewhere on the Mac.

apps.summary: A menu-bar app that lists every app here, installs any of them without the Open Anyway step, and updates them all.
apps.tagline: Install any of these apps in one click, and keep them all up to date.

apps.alternativeTo: Vernier Graphical Analysis and Logger Pro
apps.internet: Only Google Sheets, to read the cells you graph, and update checks
apps.name: Straightedge
apps.needs: Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, and Google Sheets. Add its extension once with Load unpacked: the app shows how

notes: First release: physics graphs from Google Sheets data, with error bars, one-click linearising, IB max/min lines through every error bar, the gradient and intercept with uncertainties and units, a large view for the board, and a guide for teachers and students.

apps.summary: Select your lab data in a Google Sheet and click Graph: Straightedge draws it in a panel beside the sheet, with error bars from your uncertainty columns, a best-fit line, and the steepest and shallowest lines through every error bar, then gives the gradient and intercept with their uncertainties and units. Linearise in one click (y², x², √x, 1/x, log–log), work out g or k from the gradient, open the graph large for the board, and copy it into a lab report. Made for IB and AP physics; everything is worked out on your computer, and a 14-page guide comes in the zip.
apps.tagline: Physics graphs from Google Sheets, with error bars and max/min lines.

apps.alternativeTo: Vernier Video Analysis, Graphical Analysis and Tracker
apps.internet: Only for Google Drive, if you sign in, and for update checks
apps.name: Strobe
apps.needs: A Vernier Go Direct sensor for sensor experiments (Bluetooth, or USB on the Mac)

notes: Sensor experiments: collect data from Vernier Go Direct sensors over Bluetooth, or USB on the Mac. File › New Sensor Experiment (Command-N).
Time Based runs with a trigger, Events with Entry (type a value such as a mass or volume for each point), Selected Events, and photogate timing (gate, pendulum, pulse, picket fence).
Compare runs on one graph; analyse a stretch with the integral (impulse), statistics, a tangent or a fit, with IB error bars and max/min lines.
Pretend sensors to try it without one, and sensor experiments open on the iPhone too.
A 19-page guide for teachers and students comes in the download.

apps.summary: Open a video of something moving, set the scale and the axes, and click the object on each frame, or draw a box round it and let Strobe track it. You get position, velocity and acceleration in a table and on graphs, with fits, uncertainties and max/min gradient lines, energy and momentum for collisions, and a strobe-picture worksheet with an answer key. Sensor experiments collect data from Vernier Go Direct sensors over Bluetooth or USB: time-based runs with a trigger, events with typed values such as masses or volumes, and photogate timing, with integrals, statistics, tangents and fits. Projects are .strobe files, kept on your Mac or in your Google Drive.
apps.tagline: Track motion in video or collect Vernier sensor data, then graph and fit it.

apps.name: Throw

notes: A throw://open link opens Throw's menu, so Shunt can offer a TV when you send a window to the other screen and there isn't one yet.

apps.summary: Connect to nearby TVs, and to Apple TVs over direct Wi-Fi where the network keeps them apart, as a mirror, an extra screen or a window. Drag the TV around an arrangement map, pick a resolution, and remember each room.
apps.tagline: AirPlay to TVs from the menu bar, then arrange them.

apps.name: Tuck

notes: Launch at Login now always opens this copy in Applications. Before, a Mac could keep opening an old copy at login.

apps.summary: Choose which apps' icons to tuck away; the arrow (click, hover or a shortcut) shows everything for a moment. Search opens any icon's menu. Needs macOS 27.
apps.tagline: Tidy the menu bar. Tuck icons away behind an arrow.

apps.name: WordCell
apps.summary: Word, Grid and Deck tabs in one window, saved together in one file.
apps.tagline: Documents, spreadsheets and slides in one app.
